text: Prior to the COVID-19 pandemic, the City of Toronto’s independent live performance venues, including independent theatre spaces as well as drag bars, have been long-suffering. Now through the uncertainty of the pandemic, it is impossible to financially plan for the future. With exorbitant commercial rents, and the unpredictable nature of the pandemic, and the pressures of development in the downtown core it is impossible for small performance venues to survive. These live performances venues include drag bars, community cultural hubs, and safe performance spaces for the LGBTQ2S+ community. Drag performers are a critical component of queer culture, and their performance venues often double as bars, cafes, restaurants, and even book stores. City Council on April 7 and 8, 2021, adopted the following: 1. City Council request the Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer and the General Manager, Economic Development and Culture to review and explore the feasibility of expanding the Creative Co-Location Facilities Property Tax Subclasses to include independent live performance venues, such as drag bars and small independent theatre and consider the impact, eligibility, administrative efficiency and alternative measures and report back to City Council in the fourth quarter of 2021 on any proposed changes. 2.
